chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Hamid, from Abu Jameela, from Al-Hasan ibn Ziyad, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
When a man copulates with his wife, then she claims the dower and he says, 'I have given you,' then upon him is the proof and upon him is the oath.
ai.seo_question: What is the burden of proof when a husband and wife disagree on whether the dower was paid after consummation?
ai.summary: This ruling from al-Kafi highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle of 'al-bayyuna 'ala al-muddi' (proof on the claimant) combined with 'al-yamin li-man anqada' (oath for the one who denies), ensuring that the husband's denial is substantiated by an oath after the wife provides evidence. It reflects the practical application of evidentiary standards in family law, balancing the wife's right to financial security with the husband's need for legal protection against false claims. This dual requirement underscores the Shia emphasis on procedural justice in marital disputes.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Ahmad, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Hameed, from Abu Jameela, from Al Hassan Bin Ziyad, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘When the man copulates with his wife, then he pays the dower and said, ‘I have given you’, so upon him would be the (burden of) the proof, and upon him would be the swearing (of an oath)’.
en.sarwar: 4. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Muhammad ibn Ahmad from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Hamid from abu Jamilah from al- Hassan ibn Ziyad who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
When a man goes to bed with his wife then she asks for her mahr (dower) and he says that he has paid, he must present testimony and take an oath.’”
